challenges.reason: Norwood explains that, when it is uncertain whether two actions involve the same cause of action, the test is whether the facts essential to maintenance or the evidence sustaining both actions are the same; different facts or proof mean the earlier judgment does not bar the later action. That supplies guidance on whether claims are sufficiently factually connected for res judicata purposes.
challenges.sourcePassage: "[I]f it is doubtful whether a second action is for the same cause of action as the first, the test generally applied is to consider the identity of facts essential to their maintenance, or whether the same evidence would sustain both. If the same facts or evidence would sustain both, the two actions are considered the same... If, however, the two actions rest upon different states of facts, or if different proofs would be required to sustain the two actions, a judgment in one is no bar to the maintenance of the other."
